incidents.cause: The pilot stalled the airplane during a go-around.  Contributing to the accident included the pilot's improper in-flight decision, the tailwind landing, and the pilot's failure to put the carburetor Heat to "OFF" during the go-around.
The student pilot's failure to maintain separation from a hangar building while taxiing. Contributing to the accident was the hangar building.
The fatigue failure of the No. 1 cylinder exhaust valve spring retainer due to air trapped in the lubrication system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
The fatigue failure of an exhaust valve spring retainer due to air trapped in the lubrication system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed on final approach, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control during the landing attempt and the flight instructor’s inadequate remedial action.
The loss of engine power due to three stuck exhaust valves.

The pilot’s improper fuel planning and his failure to adequately monitor the fuel level during flight, which resulted in fuel exhaustion, and a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s lack of attention performing the task, which led to a loss of situational awareness
The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane attitude control during the landing, resulting in a hard landing.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.

The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing, and his subsequent failure to maintain directional control during landing with a gusting crosswind, which resulted in a ground-loop.
The pilot’s failure to maintain an appropriate descent rate during approach, which resulted in landing short of the runway threshold.
